cards.explanation: The answer is his love of this world. Paul says it straight: "…Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica." That's the reason the text gives, so I won't add any more to it. Paul doesn't say how it felt for him, but I think it stung, friends, since Demas had been counted among his fellow workers (Philemon 1:24).

The answer is Luke. "Only Luke is with me," Paul says. Luke is the beloved physician (Colossians 4:14), and he's the one still with Paul. Three people gone, and one friend still with him. I think that friend meant a whole lot.

The answer is that Mark is useful in the ministry. Paul has just listed who's gone, and he says only Luke is with him. Then comes the ask: "Get Mark and bring him with you…" His reason is "…he is useful to me in the ministry." I think that's a big thing for Paul to say, friends, because it's the same Mark who has a rough spot in his history with Paul, and here Paul is asking for him by name.
The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus." Demas left Paul, but Paul himself sent Tychicus. Different road, different reason.

The answer is Lord. Paul says, "The Lord will repay him according to his deeds." Paul doesn't say he'll do it himself. He leaves it with the Lord, and I think that's a peaceful place to leave it, friends.

The answer is that Alexander has strongly opposed their message. Paul says Alexander "…has vigorously opposed our message." Notice the word "our," friends. Paul and Timothy share this message, so a warning to be careful of the man comes with it.

The answers are deserted and stood. Paul says, "…everyone deserted me." That's a lonely moment to stand up in front of people, friends. I think it was a hard one, and then Paul turns to the good part: "But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me…" Everyone else left, and the Lord stayed, so that the message would be fully proclaimed (2 Timothy 4:17).

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "May it not be charged against them." Just before that he says, "At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me." They left him, and he still asks that it not be held against them.

The answer is all the Gentiles. Paul says the Lord strengthened him "…so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it." Gentiles are people who aren't Jews, friends. That's the whole reach he mentions.

The answer is that the Lord will bring him safely into the heavenly kingdom. Paul says the Lord will rescue him from every evil action and "…bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom." Paul is looking ahead to that kingdom, friends. Then he adds, "To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen."

The answer is that he was left sick in Miletus. Paul says, "…Trophimus I left sick in Miletus." The text doesn't say more than that. I think it's a gentle reminder, friends, that Paul's circle was dealing with real troubles.
The answer is winter. Paul says, "Make every effort to come to me before winter." He first asked back in verse 9, and now he adds a deadline. That's the word to hold onto, friends.
The answer is True, friends. The very last words are "Grace be with you all." Right before that Paul writes, "The Lord be with your spirit." He ends the letter with grace.
